name: Haystack Enterprise AI – chat and chat stream as AI Agent tools

options.systemMessage: You have no knowledge of your own about our product, documentation, or data. For every user message that could benefit from factual information, your very first action must be a tool call — do not write any text, explanation, or stated plan before calling it. Call "Chat With Knowledge Base" when the user is following up on something said earlier in this conversation, or explicitly wants to discuss, talk through, or get guidance on a topic. Call "One-off Chat" for a standalone question that doesn't depend on earlier turns. If the user names a tool directly, or asks to "chat" or "have a conversation" about something, honor that instead of guessing. Only write your final answer after the tool result comes back, and base it only on that result. Only skip the tool call for messages that need no factual information at all, such as greetings or thanks.

parameters.toolDescription: Ask the knowledge base a single, self-contained question. Use this for one-off lookups, not for open-ended or conversational requests.
parameters.query: ={{ $fromAI('Query', 'The question to ask the knowledge base', 'string') }}

parameters.toolDescription: Ask the support chat service a question when the request calls for a more conversational, explanatory answer (e.g. guidance, reasoning, or elaboration over the knowledge base) rather than a single fact lookup.
parameters.query: ={{ $fromAI('Query', 'The question or message to send to the support chat service', 'string') }}

parameters.content:
### Chat and Chat (Streaming) as AI Agent tools

Haystack Enterprise AI sets `usableAsTool: true`, so any operation can be wired into an AI Agent's Tool input instead of the main flow — the agent decides whether and when to call it, and with what arguments, based on the user's message.

This workflow adds two separate tool instances of the node, one per operation, so the agent can pick whichever fits the request:

1. **One-off Chat** (Chat) — a one-off question. Search Session ID stays empty, so this call does not continue a conversation.
2. **Chat With Knowledge Base** (Chat/Streaming) — a conversational-style ask against a chat-tuned service. Good for open-ended or explanatory requests.

Each tool's **Query** field uses `$fromAI(...)`, so the agent supplies the actual query text at call time rather than it being fixed by you. Each tool's **Description** (`descriptionType`/`toolDescription`, shown once a node is connected as a tool) tells the agent when to reach for it — tune the wording to match what your own services actually do.

**Giving the chat tool its own search session.** The Chat (Streaming) endpoint needs a **Search Session ID** to have any conversation history of its own on the deepset side — leave it empty and each call starts a new session instead of continuing the previous one. Since the agent may call the "Chat With Knowledge Base" tool more than once across a conversation, this workflow reuses the same session-management pattern as [`chat-with-search-session.json`](./chat-with-search-session.json), just running *before* the Agent instead of before a direct Chat call: **Look Up Search Session** checks workflow static data for a session already mapped to this n8n chat session; **Has Search Session?** branches to skip straight to the Agent if one exists, or through **Create Search Session** (Search Session resource, Create operation), **Merge** and **Remember Search Session** (stores the mapping) if not. Both branches converge on the Agent's main input with `searchSessionId` set on the item, and the **Chat With Knowledge Base** tool's **Search Session ID** field reads it back via `={{ $json.searchSessionId }}` — tool node expressions see the same input item as the node they're attached to, so this resolves correctly no matter which branch ran. As before, static data is workflow-scoped and fine for a demo, but swap it for a real data store in production.

Note this deepset-side session (Chat's own history of queries/answers) is a separate thing from the Agent's own **Simple Memory** (the Agent's own record of the conversation, used to make sense of follow-ups when deciding what to ask a tool) — both exist here and serve different layers.

**Why there's a Merge node before Remember Search Session.** Create Search Session's output only carries `search_session_id` — it doesn't pass through the original item's `sessionId`/`chatInput`. The obvious fix is to have the Code node reach back with `$('Look Up Search Session').item.json`, and that's what an earlier version of this workflow did — but a Code node using `$('Node Name')` needs an extra round trip to the main process under n8n's external Task Runner, and in testing that round trip hung for the full 300-second task timeout before erroring. Recombining both branches' data with a **Merge** node (Combine, by Position) ahead of the Code node instead means it only ever touches its own `$json`, with no cross-node lookup at all.

**Why the system message is so blunt.** The underlying model already has broad general knowledge and will happily answer from that instead of calling a tool, especially for questions that sound generic. n8n's Agent node doesn't expose a "force tool call" setting (unlike the raw OpenAI `tool_choice` API parameter), so the only lever here is the prompt: telling the agent it has *no* knowledge of its own and *must* call a tool is what actually gets tool calls to happen reliably. Loosen this wording only once you've confirmed tool calls are firing as expected.

**Picking One-off Chat vs. Chat With Knowledge Base.** A standalone question goes to One-off Chat. A follow-up, or a request to discuss or get guidance, goes to Chat With Knowledge Base. If the user names a tool directly, honor that. To exercise the conversational tool while testing, ask a follow-up ("and how does that compare to what you just said about X?"), ask to discuss/get guidance ("can we talk through how to think about X?"), or name the tool ("use Chat With Knowledge Base to answer: ...").

**Node type note.** When n8n connects a `usableAsTool` node to an Agent's Tool input, it registers that instance under the node's own type name with `Tool` appended (e.g. `haystackEnterpriseAiTool`), not the plain node type — that variant is what actually carries the `ai_tool` output. Dragging the node onto the Agent's tool port from the canvas does this for you automatically; if you hand-edit or copy-paste workflow JSON instead, make sure the `type` field on any tool-connected instance has that `Tool` suffix, or it'll load as a disconnected main-flow node with no tool output at all.
